chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servants.
But He is a tyrant to the tyrants.

key_terms.الظَّالِمِينَ: The tyrants / those who are unjust to themselves
key_terms.ظَلَّامٌ: A tyrant / one who deals unjustly

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between God being unjust to the unjust and being unjust to His servants?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*), distinguishing between God's inherent justice and the self-inflicted injustice of those who reject His signs. This explanation underscores that divine punishment is not an arbitrary act of God but a consequence of human free will and self-negligence, a key tenet distinguishing Shia theology from other schools. The Imam’s statement serves as a foundational argument for the concept that God does not wrong His servants, but rather they wrong themselves through their own actions.
